chunks: From him, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) [from his father (from his father, peace be upon him), that he said:

To a man who had spoken to him with a lengthy speech, so he said: 'O man, you belittle speech and consider it insignificant. Know that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not send His messengers with whom He sent gold or silver, but He sent them with speech. And indeed, Allah, Glorious and Mighty, made Himself known to His creation through speech, and the indications towards Him, and the signs.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Allah send prophets with speech instead of gold and silver?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects a companion’s potential underestimation of eloquence by highlighting that divine guidance was transmitted through speech rather than material wealth. This underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Quran and prophetic traditions rely on the power of language and clear signs (dalalat) to convey God's essence and will to humanity. It elevates speech from mere communication to a sacred vehicle of revelation and epistemological clarity.
